```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
rmd_file <- normalizePath(
  knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE), winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE
)
realdata_root <- dirname(rmd_file)
processed_dir <- file.path(realdata_root, "processed")

required_files <- file.path(
  processed_dir,
  c(
    "analysis_manifest.csv", "group_counts.csv", "full_matrix_audit.csv",
    "excluded_missing_rnaseq.csv", "selected_features_top2000_annotated.csv"
  )
)
if (!all(file.exists(required_files))) {
  stop("Processed GDSC audit files are incomplete.")
}

manifest <- read.csv(file.path(processed_dir, "analysis_manifest.csv"))
group_counts <- read.csv(file.path(processed_dir, "group_counts.csv"))
matrix_audit <- read.csv(file.path(processed_dir, "full_matrix_audit.csv"))
excluded <- read.csv(file.path(processed_dir, "excluded_missing_rnaseq.csv"))
features <- read.csv(
  file.path(processed_dir, "selected_features_top2000_annotated.csv")
)
```

# Purpose

This document records the cleaning and processing steps used to construct the
GDSC2 gemcitabine dataset in the course report. The statistical unit is a
cancer cell line. The prediction target is `LN_IC50` for gemcitabine, and the
predictors are RNA-sequencing expression measurements from Cell Model
Passports. Lower `LN_IC50` indicates greater drug sensitivity.

# Source data

The response file is the official GDSC2 fitted dose-response workbook dated
27 October 2023. Cell-line identifiers, cancer labels, and RNA-seq download
links come from Cell Model Passports. Unmodified source files are retained in
`raw/gdsc/`, and the per-model expression archives are retained in
`raw/rnaseq/`. File checksums and source URLs are documented alongside the
raw data.

# Cleaning workflow

## 1. Construct the analysis manifest

The manifest retains gemcitabine records from pancreatic cancer, colorectal
cancer, gastric cancer, ovarian cancer, and non-small-cell lung cancer. Each
GDSC record is joined one-to-one to a Cell Model Passports identifier. Records
with missing outcomes, duplicate model identifiers, or discordant cancer labels
cause the script to stop rather than being silently removed.

```{bash manifest-command, eval=FALSE}
python gdsc_real_data/scripts/01_prepare_manifest.py
```

## 2. Download and validate RNA-seq archives

RNA-seq files are downloaded from the official Cell Model Passports endpoint.
Every ZIP archive is opened and its expected CSV schema is checked. Download
status is checkpointed after each model. Models without a valid harmonized
RNA-seq archive are excluded before modeling, and the reason is retained in
`processed/excluded_missing_rnaseq.csv`. No pancreatic target model is excluded.

```{bash download-command, eval=FALSE}
python gdsc_real_data/scripts/02_download_rnaseq.py
```

## 3. Build the modeling matrices without target leakage

Expression is converted to `log2(TPM + 1)`. Genes must have TPM greater than 1
in at least 20 percent of external models. Eligible genes are ranked by
variance among external models only. The 1,000- and 2,000-gene matrices are
then formed using that fixed ranking. Pancreatic outcomes and pancreatic
expression measurements are not used to define the feature set.

```{bash matrix-command, eval=FALSE}
python gdsc_real_data/scripts/03_build_matrix.py
python gdsc_real_data/scripts/09_build_full_matrix.py
```

# Audit summaries

```{r group-count-table}
knitr::kable(
  group_counts,
  caption = "Cancer groups before expression-file exclusions."
)
```

```{r matrix-audit-table}
knitr::kable(
  matrix_audit,
  caption = "Final 2,000-gene matrix audit."
)
```

```{r exclusion-table}
knitr::kable(
  excluded[, c("model_id", "model_name", "cancer_group", "status", "message")],
  caption = "Models excluded because a valid public RNA-seq archive was unavailable."
)
```

The final matrix contains `r matrix_audit$value[matrix_audit$item == "models"]`
models, including `r matrix_audit$value[matrix_audit$item == "target_models"]`
pancreatic target models and
`r matrix_audit$value[matrix_audit$item == "external_models"]` external models.
The feature log contains `r nrow(features)` externally selected genes and
retains the Ensembl identifier, gene symbol, external-sample variance,
expression-frequency filter, and rank for every feature.

# Modeling and reproducibility

The model runners consume only the fixed processed matrices and saved fold
assignments. The primary experiment, audit, refined target-domain alpha
experiment, and report figures can be regenerated in this order:

```{bash modeling-commands, eval=FALSE}
Rscript gdsc_real_data/scripts/10_run_full_experiment.R
python gdsc_real_data/scripts/11_audit_full_experiment.py
Rscript gdsc_real_data/scripts/12_make_full_figures.R
Rscript gdsc_real_data/scripts/15_run_conservative_alpha_experiment.R
python gdsc_real_data/scripts/16_audit_conservative_alpha.py
Rscript gdsc_real_data/scripts/17_make_conservative_figures.R
```

The experiment evaluates prediction of in-vitro cell-line sensitivity. It is
not a clinical validation study and does not establish a treatment biomarker.
